claims.text: Two threads may write one 16-token block without conflict: items of one block that are not consecutive fall into several units, and each writer touches only its own token's bytes. In an unconverted block that is the token's own 256-byte row-major row (store_row_major, 4 whole lines); in a converted block it is the token's 64 pair slots, written by 4 scatters of 16 dwords (store_row). When a run fills the block, the block gets one full-line store per pair row (store_block).

The page converts a block once; an entry for a block already converted (a row saved again) returns CONVERTED_FALSE and the bool is discarded.
It runs on the main thread after wait_for_coop_gof: the cooperative GOF staging gather of an earlier minibatch is the last reader that can still hold the block's rows row-major.
The storage reference is taken at the save (k_storage_of), so a storage view change between the save and the forward end cannot redirect the conversion.

The run also ends at a page change (3290) and at a block change (3292), not only at a repeated offset (3294); the item that ended the run starts the next one because t is not advanced on break.

proposed_lead_bullets: Contract: stores the K rows (every KV head) of items[task_begin, task_end) into slot; marks, saved-row bits of partial runs and credits are not touched here. save_k_impl does them after every store is done.
Row-major slots (layout_on false): one row store per token and KV head through page::k(slot, kv_head, j).set, the old per-token loop moved here from the marks loop.

VNNI slots: a run collects consecutive KV items of one block c of one page. An item without KV work is skipped and does not end the run; a page change, a block change or the same offset twice ends it, and that item starts the next run.

A run of 16 covers its block (TRON_ASSERT present == FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF): page::set_k_block per KV head, then note_k_block_saved publishes the 16 row bits and the block bit. Any thread of a shared window may do this.
A shorter run goes through page::set_k_row per token and KV head: the row-major tail block, or the VNNI column when the block is converted already (set_k_row decides from the block bit).
A non-bf16 K buffer is converted to bf16 on the stack first (conv, 16 rows of head_size, 64-byte aligned); a bf16 buffer is read in place through k_source_row.

claims.text: tron: the inference server program this file belongs to. model.hpp holds the parts common to all tron models, which do not vary across plugins.

fields.definition: The inference server program under test; model.hpp holds the common parts of all tron models.

claims.text: Plugin, generated vs handwritten: a plugin is one model's code. Generated plugins come from the ingest tool (TronCpp.hs) and have run() for main and run_main_help for the helpers; handwritten plugins and the unit tests call save_k with the defaults (n_workers == 1), so they never share.

claims.text: book: the unit of KV memory allocation. The book owns the memory for a requested number of pages and hands out page references on demand.

fields.definition: The struct that owns the KV memory for a request number of pages; a page is a lightweight reference to a section of a book.

claims.text: page: 64 tokens (page_size = 64) of KV for every slot and KV head. page_of(token_id) returns the page holding a token and offset_in_page gives the token's offset 0..63 inside it.

fields.definition: A page holds 64 tokens of K and V per slot and KV head. page_of(tok) returns *token_pages[tok]; offset_in_page(tok) returns tok.i - lo, the token's offset in the page.

claims.text: slot (kv_slot_id): selects persistent KV storage described by kv_slot_specs. save_k takes the slot from operation.binding.kv_slot.

fields.definition: A kv_slot_id selects persistent KV storage described by kv_slot_specs; one attention operation writes one slot.

claims.text: KV head: one key/value head of the model. A token has geometry.kv.n_kv_heads K rows of geometry.kv.head_size values each, and save_k stores one row per (token, KV head).

fields.definition: One key/value head; geometry.kv.n_kv_heads per token, each K row geometry.kv.head_size bf16 values (128 for the VNNI layout).

claims.text: EAGLE: EAGLE-style speculation stores the validation model's final embedding alongside the KV page. The page keeps one extra K layout state entry for the EAGLE storage, and k_storage_of resolves slot zero to it while the EAGLE view is active.

fields.definition: A speculation scheme whose KV storage has its own page entry; k_state_ix maps slot zero to the EAGLE entry while the EAGLE view is active, and k_storage_ref carries that resolved index.

claims.text: plane, panel, pair row: a plane is K for one KV head of one page (64 tokens x 128 dimensions of bf16 = 16 KiB). A panel is one (dimension step, token block) of the VNNI plane, 16 pair rows of 64 bytes = 1 KiB = one AMX B tile; a pair row is one 64-byte line holding one dimension pair of 16 consecutive tokens.

fields.definition: Plane = K of one KV head of one page (16 KiB). Panel = 16 pair rows of 64 bytes for one 32-dimension step and one 16-token block (1 KiB, one AMX B tile). Pair row = one 64-byte line = one dimension pair of 16 tokens. The block save writes each pair row with one full-line store.

claims.text: VNNI: Vector Neural Network Instructions layout. The two values of a dimension pair of one token are stored next to each other and one 64-byte row holds that pair for 16 consecutive tokens; it is the B-operand layout of the AMX tile multiply.

fields.definition: The pair-interleaved K layout: dimension pair of one token adjacent, one 64-byte row per dimension pair for 16 consecutive tokens; the AMX tile-multiply B-operand layout.

claims.text: AMX: Advanced Matrix Extensions, the CPU tile instruction set. The AMX QK kernel reads a VNNI page directly as its B operand.

fields.definition: Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set; qk_vnni_128x4 reads the VNNI plane as its B operand.

claims.text: AVX-512: the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set. The VNNI reader k_vnni::qk_group and the block save (store_block, masked 64-byte stores) are AVX-512 code.

fields.definition: The 512-bit vector instruction set; used by store_block's register transpose and masked stores and by the qk_group reader.

claims.text: bf16: the 16-bit brain floating-point format. K rows are stored as bf16; store_k_block converts any other activation type to bf16 on the stack (conv) first.

fields.definition: 16-bit brain floating-point; the storage type of K rows. A non-bf16 K buffer is converted on the stack before the store.

claims.text: staging and DMA: gof::populate copies the K/V rows of a GOF into a staging buffer, and DMA (direct memory access) moves that buffer to the FPGA card. The staging gather of an earlier minibatch is the reader that can still hold a block's rows row-major, so the conversion waits for the forward end.

fields.definition: Staging = the buffer gof::populate fills with a GOF's K/V rows; DMA = direct memory access, the engine that moves the buffer to the card. wait_for_coop_gof drains the cooperative staging work at the forward end.

claims.text: minibatch (struct batch, often named q_batch): a subset of the forward's token jobs, held in items. A pass runs each minibatch through every layer, and save_k runs once per (layer, pass) for a minibatch.

fields.definition: struct batch is one minibatch; q_batch->items is its token jobs (token_job_id) in order. save_k's loops and the unit table index items by position.

claims.text: grain: tokens are first split into grains of at most minibatch_grain_size = 8, then grains are merged greedily into minibatches. A 16-token block can therefore be split across two minibatches of one pass.

fields.definition: A group of at most 8 tokens (minibatch_grain_size), the unit the batcher merges into minibatches; a partner job moved to the end of a grain can make a block's items non-consecutive.

claims.text: main helpers: the app-pool threads that help the main thread; they occupy the first num_workers() - n_attn_workers pool workers. The generated run_main_help runs them with worker_ix 1 .. n_workers - 1, and n_workers = 1 + n_main_helpers.

fields.definition: Helper threads of the main thread. worker_ix 0 is main, 1 .. n_workers - 1 are helpers; run_main_help(q_batches, worker_ix, n_workers) is the generated helper body that emits a save_k call for every KV-writing attention statement.

claims.text: attention workers: the last n_attn_workers pool workers. They run the attention sections and, when idle between layers, drain the cooperative GOF queue (help_drain_gof); they take no part in the K store window.

fields.definition: Pool workers that run the per-layer attention plan; their pending sections wait behind save_k, and they drain GOF staging work when idle.

claims.text: tree lock: the scheduler's global tree_lock over the token tree. Page operations that transpose blocks in place between forward passes (clear_kv_complete_at, copy_from) rely on it: no forward pass reads the book meanwhile.

fields.definition: The global lock the scheduler holds while it edits the token tree and the KV pages between forward passes.

claims.text: acquire / release, fetch_add / fetch_or: std::memory_order tags and atomic read-modify-write operations. A release write publishes every earlier write of its thread to a reader whose acquire load sees it; fetch_add returns the old value (the unit claim on next_unit) and fetch_or sets bits (the page's row and block bits).

fields.definition: In the window: opened is incremented with release by main and loaded with acquire by helpers; next_unit.fetch_add uses acq_rel; finished is incremented with release by a helper and loaded with acquire by main. The page's note_k_block_saved uses fetch_or on k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_.

claims.text: TRON_K_VNNI and layout_on: TRON_K_VNNI is the CMake option (default OFF, requires TRON_AMX_DISPATCH) that stores the K plane of every 128-dimension head in the VNNI layout. k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> is true only for head_size 128 under that option; store_k_block, k_store_shared and the recording loop branch on it at compile time.

fields.definition: Build-time gate of the VNNI K layout; a property of the storage geometry, not of the query type or AMX availability, so every reader and writer of a slot sees the same layout.

claims.text: dotter: the per-token dot-product loop of self_attention.hpp (struct dotter in kernels/dotter.hpp). It scores row-major K rows, including the rows of a row-major tail block read through row_major_row.

fields.definition: The AVX software reader for row-major K: one dot product per (query head, token) through a typed row view.

claims.text: qk_group: k_vnni::qk_group, the AVX-512 reader of the VNNI layout. It scores one query group against the live tokens of one page with one token per vector lane, so there is no per-token gather and no horizontal reduction.

fields.definition: The software score reader for VNNI blocks (partial pages, hosts without AMX, the kill switch); tokens of a row-major block keep their live bit clear and go to the dotter.

claims.text: qk_vnni_128x4: amx_attn_h128g4::qk_vnni_128x4, the AMX QK kernel that reads a whole VNNI page as its B operand and computes S = Q . K^T in the orientation the softmax wants.

fields.definition: The AMX kernel for a dense VNNI page; it replaces qk_rowmajor_128x4's transposing store.

claims.text: work unit: a run of consecutive items of one minibatch inside one 16-token block of one page with the same token_jobs_do_kv value, items[unit_start[u], unit_start[u + 1]). Threads claim units with fetch_add on next_unit; writers of two units of one block touch disjoint token lanes (masked stores).

fields.definition: The claimable piece of a shared K store. unit_start has max_minibatch_size + 1 entries; n_units counts the units of the open window; next_unit is the claim counter on its own cache line.

claims.text: window: one shared save_k of a minibatch per (layer, pass), described by the fields of batch::k_store_window (next_unit, opened, finished, n_units, unit_start, helper_windows). Main opens it by incrementing opened, each helper joins its W-th window, and main closes it when finished reaches n_workers - 1.

fields.definition: The per-minibatch protocol state of the shared K store. opened counts windows opened in the pass; helper_windows[worker_ix] counts the windows a helper entered; finished counts helpers done with the open window.

claims.text: token_id vs token_job_id: a token_id indexes the whole token tree resident in the system (global). A token_job_id indexes the tokens this forward runs (local); token_jobs maps a job to its token.

fields.definition: token_id = global tree position (changes every compute_forward_args); token_job_id = position in this forward's job list; token_jobs[ix] gives the job's token_id.

claims.text: 16-token block (k_store_block): k_store_block = k_vnni::BLOCK_TOKENS_16 = 16. A page's 64 tokens form 4 blocks; block c covers page offsets 16 c .. 16 c + 15.

fields.definition: The unit of the VNNI layout and of the shared store: 16 consecutive page offsets. 64-byte line / (2 values x 2 bytes) = 16 tokens per pair row.

claims.text: row-major tail block: a 16-token block holds its rows row-major (256 contiguous bytes per token, inside the block's own 4 panels) until all 16 rows are saved and the block is converted in place. A row-major block and a VNNI block occupy the same 4 KiB.

fields.definition: The pre-conversion form of a block: token t of block c owns 256 bytes at row_major_row(); the store writes 4 whole lines per token instead of a 64-line scatter.

claims.text: k_rows_saved_ and k_vnni_blocks_: per (page, storage slot) the page keeps one bit per page offset for saved K rows and one bit per block for converted blocks. A set block bit implies the block's 16 row bits; a block whose 16 row bits are set but whose block bit is clear is complete and waits for conversion.

fields.definition: Two atomic bit sets per storage slot (plus one EAGLE entry): saved rows (uint64_t, one bit per offset) and converted blocks (uint8_t, one bit per block). Every reader and writer of a row takes the layout from the converted-block bit.

claims.text: k_storage_ref: a storage slot offset plus the index of its K layout state. save_k takes it at the save with k_storage_of, so a view change between the save and the forward end cannot redirect the conversion.

fields.definition: struct { kv_storage_offset offset; size_t state_ix; }; k_storage_of(slot) resolves a logical slot under the current view (the EAGLE entry for the EAGLE storage).

claims.text: pending_k_blocks_: the deferred conversion list, one (pg, storage, block) entry per block that this pass completed through runs shorter than a block, for operations the hardware attention does not score. save_k fills it on main; convert_pending_k_blocks drains it at the forward end.

fields.definition: std::vector<pending_k_block>; drained after wait_for_coop_gof, the first point where no reader of the pass is left.

claims.text: TRON_ASSERT: a checked condition that aborts the process (tron_abort, then std::abort) with a formatted message when false. The window's join watchdog, the worker-index check and the unit-table bound are TRON_ASSERTs.

fields.definition: Abort-on-false assertion macro with a fmt message; it is not disabled in release builds here.

claims.text: _mm_pause: the x86 pause instruction, from <immintrin.h>. The window's wait loops execute it between polls of opened (helper) and finished (main).

fields.definition: A spin-wait hint that slows the polling loop and saves power; k_join_clock_spins counts these loops between clock reads.

claims.text: channel (K channel): the producer/consumer interlock over a buffer (Note [Channel design]): prepare on main, start_writing/finish_writing per producer, start_reading per consumer. Main waits for every token's K channel before save_k, so the rows a helper reads from ks are ready.

fields.definition: A phase-tracked buffer whose readiness latches keep producers and consumers in step; the channel phase cannot advance while main is inside save_k.

claims.text: cache line (cache_line_size): 64 bytes. next_unit and opened each sit on their own cache line (alignas(cache_line_size)) so a unit claim does not invalidate the line the waiting threads poll.

fields.definition: std::hardware_destructive_interference_size (64 bytes); the unit of memory the CPU caches move, used to keep polled and claimed counters apart.

claims.text: token lane and FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF (__mmask16): a 16-bit mask with one bit per token of a block (bit t = page offset 16 c + t); FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF means all 16 present. store_block masks its line stores to the present lanes, so two threads can write one block on disjoint lanes without conflict.

fields.definition: Token t of a block owns lane t (column t % 16) of every pair row; the mask selects which lanes a store writes. store_k_block asserts the mask is full for a run of 16.

claims.text: mark_k_complete and credit_gof_save: mark_k_complete adds 1 to the page's per-(offset, slot) save counter kv_saves_ (save_k and save_v each add 1; 2 means both saved). credit_gof_save counts the K save toward its GOF's counter and enqueues a completed GOF on the cooperative drain queue.

fields.definition: The per-token completion marks and GOF credits that stay on main after the join, in q_batch->items order.

claims.text: wait_for_coop_gof and help_drain_gof: attention workers drain the cooperative GOF queue when idle (help_drain_gof). wait_for_coop_gof is the forward-end barrier on main that drains the rest and waits for in-flight submits; convert_pending_k_blocks runs right after it.

fields.definition: The cooperative GOF dispatch: save_k enqueues a completed GOF, idle workers populate and DMA-submit it, main finishes the tail at the forward end.

claims.text: set_k_block and set_k_row: page::set_k_block stores the 16 rows of one block at once (store_block transposes them in registers and writes each pair row with one 64-byte store); the result is bit-identical to set_k_row per token. page::set_k_row is the layout-agnostic single-row store: VNNI column when the block is converted (store_row), row-major block otherwise (store_row_major), memcpy for a row-major slot.

fields.definition: The two K store entry points of the page used by store_k_block; set_k_block takes 16 native row pointers (rows[t] = offset c * 16 + t), set_k_row takes one const_k_row_view.

claims.text: note_k_row_saved and note_k_block_saved: note_k_row_saved sets the row's bit in k_rows_saved_ and returns true when the block now has all 16 rows saved and is not converted yet (true again for a row saved again into such a block, false for a converted block). note_k_block_saved sets the 16 row bits and the block bit after a whole-block save, from any thread of a shared window, after the last KV head.

fields.definition: The page's bit publishers: per row on main (recording loop), per block from store_k_block (any thread). A row-major slot keeps no bits and note_k_row_saved returns false.

claims.text: k_block_to_vnni_at: converts block c of every KV head of a storage slot from row-major to VNNI in place when its 16 rows are saved and it is not converted yet, then sets the block bit; returns whether it converted. Main thread only, at a point where no reader of the block runs (the forward end).

fields.definition: The deferred conversion: block_to_vnni copies the 16 rows to the stack and calls store_block with FULL_BLOCK_0XFFFF; the page sets k_vnni_blocks_ bit c with release afterwards.
